search_strategy: Built two local indices early (a JSON dump of the whole Mattermost export, /tmp/gc.py for cross-channel keyword grep, /tmp/cc.py for a single channel/date-range window read) and used them almost exclusively -- no wiki page-comment or mail reads are visible for this task; the ticket's own #engineering/#pipeline/#code-review remarks were dense enough that chat alone gave the design. Strategy was keyword-sweep-then-window-read: run gc.py with a term cluster ('reasons', 'ledger', 'template padded six digit prefix', 'accumulation warmup loss_history signature trailing', 'learning_rate_at effective_warmup cosine', 'plan_steps step_ledger dataset_signature ResumePlan StepPlan'), then cc.py to read full context around each date the sweep surfaced. This found nearly everything: 44 of 47 remarks. It missed g11.r2.l7, g11.r2.l11 (facts still covered by other remarks) and, consequentially, g11.r2.l10 -- because no sweep ever used 'min_lr_ratio'/'MIN_LR_RATIO' as a search term despite the agent typing both dozens of times in its own analysis, and #code-review was never read past 2025-04-14. The agent treated the LR design as settled once the shape and the min_lr_ratio rescaling semantics were confirmed (line 3536, 4093, 4907, 5008) and did not run a final targeted sweep on the identifier itself before writing code.
end_reason: N/A -- the run completed normally: pushed, CI green, deployed (provenance.pushed=1, provenance.ci_green=1, provenance.deployed=1), open_feature and 8 of 9 hidden facts scored 1. Only g11.r2.rule scored 0, on a single narrow sub-assertion (keyword-only-ness of min_lr_ratio) inside an otherwise fully correct implementation.
notable: The agent's own shipped docstring for canonical_reasons explicitly names the herring it avoids ('rather than alphabetical, which used to put final ahead of interval and read as though the run had ended before it looped') -- strong evidence it correctly resolved herring vs. reversal for r1 (content_json msg 175).

The agent independently re-derived and cross-checked every numeric LR/checkpoint value against the quoted runs (lines 5420, 5571) before writing code, which is why observability passed on both requirements despite two of its source remarks (r2.l7, r2.l11) never surfacing individually.

It even chased a parked, easy-to-miss cookbook detail (default warmup=10 on a 3-step smoke example, from g11.r2.l12) after finishing the main implementation (line 7196-7247), showing real thoroughness -- which makes the miss on g11.r2.l10 read as a search-coverage gap rather than carelessness.

The only failing assertion in the whole run is the first line of test_rule__inclusive_warmup_then_a_linear_decay_to_a_tenth_of_the_base_rate (test_r2.py:55) -- a single inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY check; every other assertion in that same test (the numeric schedule) would have passed.
